analysis: The trial completed successfully but failed to improve validation macro HR@10: 0.495 versus the stated prior 0.520 (−0.025) and baseline 0.505 (−0.010). Category HR@10 was Movies_and_TV 0.545, Industrial_and_Scientific 0.530, Electronics 0.345, and CDs_and_Vinyl 0.560. The ten-transition recency half-life did not support the proposed improvement in this run. It reduces older transitions’ contribution while preserving equal total weight per sampled user; the aggregate decline does not establish why performance worsened. Prior per-category scores were not supplied, so category-level changes cannot be determined. The supplied code implements the intended weighting, but no deterministic weighting-check results were reported.
code_summary: One independent taste-aware SASRec network and one selected checkpoint per category. Defaults: 100-item windows, 96-dimensional embeddings, two causal Transformer blocks, two attention heads, and dropout 0.25. A gated causal cumulative-history taste feature augments Transformer features; normalized embeddings, learned scale, and jointly trained item biases produce scores. Training uses sampled cross-entropy with 192 shared uniform negatives, complete train-history and positive-collision exclusion, random history windows, and per-user normalized exponential position weights with a ten-transition half-life. AdamW, seed 42, environment-controlled 200-epoch default, validation checkpoint selection, and early stopping are retained. The predictor routes all four categories and loads exactly one trained network per category; inference architecture is unchanged.
